head: NOT MERGEABLE AS CUT — 1 blocker, 7 should, 3 note. The frozen law itself holds: `check-frozen-workflows.mjs` exits 0 (299 files, 54 "use workflow" modules), `--compare-base` against both the branch base and the LIVE origin/main reports 0 hash/flag changes and additions only, the 86-file closure of the three new bodies has 0 members missing from the manifest and adds no module-level `node:` import, parts-parity and the bundle gate are green, typecheck is exit 0, and I independently reproduced `two-build-cutover-e2e` (ALL PASS: W1 parked on claraWork_v3 resumes on v3 inside build B; rollback REFUSED naming claraWork_v4 while W2 is parked), `interview-e2e` (ALL PASS), `version-cutover-e2e` (ALL PASS) and the 53 new unit cells. The blocker is a contract mismatch this cut is the first thing to make live: #639's dependent particulars question asks `useful_life_months`/`rate_bps` as `kind:"text"` (the door accepts only a JSON string) while `faParticularsAnswerSchema` types them `z.number()` (accepts only a number) — so a human who answers correctly gets their answer refused and the particulars are never applied for any depreciable asset. Measured on all three sides. Separately, `interview-kill-resume-e2e.mjs` — a registered db-live-gates step the cut did not re-run — reds deterministically on a pristine DB because `clientOnboarding_v5` answers 16 segments against a literal 15. Both are fixable before `--lock-deployed`, which has correctly not run.

findings.what: #639's dependent particulars question can never be applied for a depreciable asset. `useful_life_months` and `rate_bps` are declared `kind: "text"`, which `clara.answer_work_question` will only accept as a JSON **string**; the workflow then parses the answer with `z.number().int()`, which only accepts a **number**. The two contracts are mutually exclusive, so the only answer a human can give is the one the run refuses. Only `method:"none"` (no drivers) survives. #639 shipped the module as a contract nothing wired, so the mismatch was latent; this cut is what makes it live.
findings.evidence: Three independent measurements on the merged chain. (1) The door, via `select clara._assert_work_answer($fields,$answer,null)` on clara_wave_b_ci @55601 with the real FA_PARTICULARS_FIELDS array: `useful_life_months` as NUMBER 60 => REFUSES CLR10 {"field":"useful_life_months","reason":"invalid_answer","constraint":"text"}; as STRING "60" => ACCEPTS. The rule is 0180_work_questions.sql:477-482 (`else -- text / if jsonb_typeof(v) <> 'string' then raise 'field % must be text'`). (2) The workflow, via `node --import tsx` on the real module: `{method:'straight_line',useful_life_months:'60',residual_cents:0,start_date:'2026-01-01'}` => safeParse.success=false, `invalid_type: expected number, received string`; the same object with 60 => true. Across methods: `none` PARSES, `straight_line` and `reducing_balance` both REFUSED. (3) The UI, apps/web/lib/work/question-fields.ts:136-141 (`buildAnswer`): only a `money` field is converted to a number; every other kind is sent as `value.trim()`, i.e. a string. Net effect: `applyParticularsStepV4` returns `{ok:false, code:"CLR37", reason:"fa_particulars_invalid", message:"The depreciation particulars that came back were not the shape the register accepts, so nothing was changed."}`, the Work settles `completed` with `fixed_asset_particulars.particulars_complete:false`, and the question is already `answered` so the human cannot retry. The new cell that should have caught it asserts the wrong side: packages/runtime/tests/clara-work-v4.test.mjs:292 uses `useful_life_months: 60`. No World e2e covers the positive path (`chat-turn-v20-e2e` leg 4 only asserts particulars never reached the run, which is indistinguishable from a broken path).
findings.fix: Before the `--lock-deployed` ceremony (it has not run, so the closure is still re-cuttable): make the two drivers `kind: "money"` in FA_PARTICULARS_FIELDS — 0180's money arm is exactly `jsonb_typeof = 'number' and ~ '^-?\d+$'`, an integer JSON number, and `unit` is free text so `unit:'months'`/`'bps'` still reads correctly — OR keep the fields as `text` and accept the door's string in `faParticularsAnswerSchema` (`z.coerce.number().int().positive()` or a preprocess) so `particularsFromAnswer` still emits numbers to the door. Then re-point clara-work-v4.test.mjs:292 at the DOOR-shaped answer so the cell tests the contract rather than the schema, and re-run `check-frozen-workflows.mjs --update`.

findings.what: A registered `.github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml` step reds deterministically under clientOnboarding_v5. The test pins the literal segment count 15; v5 answers 16 because `fye_day` was added. Line 335's sibling assertion (16 business items) will be 17 for the same reason. The cut updated the fixture (`wave-b-interview-testkit.mjs` gained `fye_day: "30"`) and `interview-e2e.mjs` (+49/-25, "16-segment drive, 17 items") but not this file.
findings.evidence: Run isolated on the pristine `clara_rt_test` @55601 (the DB two-build-cutover-e2e cleans up after itself), no contention: `INTERVIEW KILL-RESUME E2E: FAIL / AssertionError: total answered equals the single-process count (15); got 16 / 16 !== 15 at interview-kill-resume-e2e.mjs:331`, EXIT=1. A first run on `clara_wave_b_ci` failed differently (90s deadline exhausted at the `fye` confirm) because that database carries leftover queued chat tasks that storm `runModelSegmentStepV20` retries against an absent OPENAI_API_KEY — the isolated run is the clean measurement. The same harness's `interview-e2e` and `version-cutover-e2e` both ALL PASS on the same rig, so this is not environmental. The cut's report §9 says the other fourteen db-live-gates legs "were green at the merge report's own run and this cut changes no migration and no DB-facing runtime code outside the three bodies" — clientOnboarding_v5 is one of the three bodies and it is what moves this count.
findings.fix: Update the two literals (15 -> 16 answered, 16 -> 17 business items) and extend the comment at :328 to name `fye_day` as the sixteenth, the way interview-e2e.mjs's own drive was updated in this commit. Re-run the leg before the integration PR.

findings.what: Every one of the eighteen new manifest entries carries `"note": ""`, including the four frozen-BY-CLOSURE library modules whose deploy order is the only thing that can hurt a deploy. This is verbatim the SHOULD #2 the previous cut's review raised (docs/plan/active/refresh-wave-2026-09-14/reports/v19-review-frozen.md: "All 8 new manifest entries carry \"note\": \"\" … Fill the notes before the ceremony") and it was not carried forward. The deploy order lives only in registry.ts's comments and the three body headers — not in the file the `--lock-deployed` ceremony reads.
findings.evidence: `node -e` over the committed manifest: 18 entries matching the new names, every one `note= "" | deployed= undefined`. Their frozen-by-closure neighbours from the v19 cut do carry it — `packages/runtime/lib/knowledge.mjs`: "DEPLOY ORDER: migration 0192 must be live BEFORE this image serves a chat turn"; `lib/periodic-adjustment-basis.ts`: "migration 0194 must be live BEFORE this image serves a chat turn"; `lib/capability-registry.mjs` and `lib/work-trace.mjs`: "migration 0195 must be live BEFORE this image runs any Work". The four new closure members that owe the same sentence are `lib/staff-expense-claim-basis.ts` (0206), `lib/accrual-basis.ts` (0207), `lib/fixed-asset-acquisition.ts` (0201) and `lib/knowledge-conflicts.mjs` (0192). Grep for DEPLOY ORDER across the eighteen files: present only in chatTurn.v20.ts:39, claraWork.v4.ts:51, clientOnboarding.v5.ts:44.
findings.fix: Fill the eighteen notes in the same shape the four existing closure notes use — provenance sentence, `DEPLOY ORDER: …`, and `NOT deploy-locked yet` — before the ceremony. `--update` preserves an existing note, so this is a one-pass hand edit followed by a re-run to a no-op.

findings.what: The particulars question's source reference deviates from #639's stanza without the deviation being recorded anywhere. The stanza specifies `p_source_ref => {kind:'fixed_asset', asset_id}`; the cut passes `{ kind: "basis_line", id: pending.assetId }`, which labels a fixed-asset id as a basis line on the surface a human answers from.
findings.evidence: 639-final.md § "Successor contract — claraWork_v4" item 1 states the stanza verbatim. The cut uses `basis_line`. Nothing constrains it at runtime: 0180_work_questions.sql:183 checks only `jsonb_typeof(source_ref) = 'object'`, and `openWorkQuestionStep` (claraWork.v2.impl.ts:305-327) passes the object straight through — the `z.enum(["document","chat_task","basis_line"])` at claraWork.v3.tools.ts:152 is a TypeScript type on the step argument, never a runtime validator, so `fixed_asset` was expressible. The human-facing consequence: apps/web/components/work/work-question-form.tsx:837-842 (`sourceRefText`) renders the kind verbatim, so the answer form says "basis_line <asset-uuid>". Grep for `basis_line` across the cut: one hit, claraWork.v4.ts:207; grep for `source_ref`/`basis_line` in reports/successors-final.md: zero hits, so the deviation is undocumented.
findings.fix: Either pass `{kind:'fixed_asset', id: pending.assetId}` as the stanza says (nothing refuses it) and lean on the Sources tab's existing unknown-kind fallback, or keep `basis_line` and say why in the file and in the report — an undocumented rename of a contract field is what makes the next reader distrust the stanza.

findings.what: The precedence rule that decides which recorded fact silently answers a question is asserted, not measured, and the database does not provide it. The docblock says "FIRST ROW WINS PER KEY, and the pack's own order is what decides it: `clara.get_knowledge_pack` returns the client's own records ahead of the firm's inherited ones". `get_knowledge_pack` sorts by `knowledge_key` alone, with no tie-break, so when a client record and a firm-wide rule both survive under one key the winner is whatever the plan emits — and the interview then SKIPS the question with it.
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0192_client_knowledge_records.sql:1502 — `select coalesce(jsonb_agg(j order by knowledge_key), '[]'::jsonb)`; the firm arm at :1509-1518 excludes a firm row only when a client row shares the same `applies_when_digest`, so a firm rule and a client exception with DIFFERENT applicability both reach the pack under one key with no defined order between them. Not hypothetical for the six keys `KNOWN_FACT_KEYS` maps: measured on the merged chain, `select knowledge_key from clara.knowledge_key_firm_eligibility` returns `accounting_basis, default_currency, reporting_framework`, and `default_currency` is `KNOWN_FACT_KEYS.currency`. The other two firm-eligible keys are among the four object-shaped folds the module deliberately excludes, so `default_currency` is the exposed one — and 0205 (#654, this wave) is what makes firm-scope defaults real. AGENTS.md rule 7: a claim about the state of the world needs a checkable source.
findings.fix: Either make the precedence explicit in the fold (prefer `scope_kind === 'client'` over `'firm'` when both are present for a mapped key, rather than relying on row order), or drop `default_currency` from `KNOWN_FACT_KEYS` until the pack's order is a guarantee, and correct the docblock either way. A cell that feeds `knownFactsFromPack` a pack with the firm row first would pin whichever rule is chosen.

findings.what: `ask_knowledge_conflict` can kill the Work instead of asking the question. The option list is built one-per-row from model-supplied `record_id`s with no de-duplication; `clara.open_work_question` refuses a choice field with duplicate option values, `openWorkQuestionStep` is not wrapped, so the throw reaches the workflow's catch and the run settles `failed`/`internal` ("This Work run failed before it could record an entry") rather than parking.
findings.evidence: 0180_work_questions.sql:394-398 — `if (select count(distinct o2->>'value') from jsonb_array_elements(f->'options') o2) <> jsonb_array_length(f->'options') then raise … constraint 'option_values_unique'`. `askKnowledgeConflictInputSchemaV4` (claraWork.v4.tools.ts:193-209) bounds `rows` at 2..4 and types `record_id` as a uuid but never requires distinctness, and `findQuestionCallV4` re-checks only `rows.length < 2`. `openWorkQuestionStep` (claraWork.v2.impl.ts:315-337) has no try/catch and claraWork.v4.ts:271 awaits it inside the try whose catch settles `failed`/`internal` at :337-344. The module's own docblock reasons about the adjacent bound in the same door — "`0180:362-479`'s field grammar is CLOSED — five kinds, 2..20 options on a choice … so the option count is 3..5 here and always inside the door's bound" — and stops one line short of the uniqueness rule beside it.
findings.fix: De-duplicate by `record_id` in `knowledgeConflictFields` (and refuse in `findQuestionCallV4` when fewer than two distinct ids survive, the same way it already refuses `rows.length < 2`), so a malformed call parks nothing rather than failing the run. Add the duplicate-id cell beside the existing option-count one.

findings.what: Two parts of #649's item 3 are absent and neither is named as a residual, while the report claims fidelity ("Per #649's stanza, and only that"). (a) The stanza asks the pre-read to seed `prior` "from `clara.get_knowledge_pack` … **plus the plan's own answered items**"; only the pack half ships, so a second run on a partly-answered plan still re-asks everything. (b) A question answered from the register is written with `answeredBy: input.startedBy`, so the durable plan item is stamped `answered_by` = a human who did not answer it, with `state='answered'` and nothing on the row saying the value came from the register.
findings.evidence: (a) 649-final.md § "Successor contract — clientOnboarding_v5" item 3: "seeding `prior` from `clara.get_knowledge_pack` (0192, already granted to `clara_runtime`) plus the plan's own answered items". In v5, `plan0.items` is read into `knownMap` for the CAS fingerprint (:88) but `prior` is initialised empty at :139 — v4's behaviour, so not a regression, but the stanza half is silently dropped and reports/successors-final.md §1 lists only the write-back as "Left open by the stanza and named here". (b) clientOnboarding.v5.ts:190-196 passes `answeredBy: input.startedBy` into `persistSegment`; `clara.onboarding_plan_items` carries a durable `answered_by` column (measured: `id, plan_id, firm_id, item_kind, item_key, question, answer, state, required_for_commit, answered_by, answered_at, …`). The only provenance is `knownEcho` streamed as an activity chunk (:203), which is not the durable record.
findings.fix: (a) Seed `prior` from the plan's answered business items before the loop, or name the omission in the report as a residual with an issue. (b) Either carry the provenance into the durable item (a `knowledge_record_id` inside the `answer` object, or a distinct `item_kind`), or state in the report that a register-sourced fact is durably attributed to the run's starter.

findings.where: the branch as a whole: frozen-workflows.json, packages/db/migrations/0199-0209, and the deploy-order sentences baked into the three frozen body headers
findings.what: The cut was measured against an origin/main that has since moved, and the stale ref hides two collisions. main retired `chatTurn_v1` under #810 (three files deleted, a NEW top-level `retired` section in the manifest, and a retirement path added to the freeze tool) and took migrations 0199-0213 for an unrelated riders batch. The branch's whole-file manifest rewrite predates all of it, and the frozen bodies hard-code deploy order by migration NUMBER, which is the thing about to be renumbered.
findings.evidence: `git fetch` moved origin/main from 4464e471 (the branch base, 2026-09-15 17:51) to 7e40e3be (2026-09-17 01:15, "riders batch 2026-09-15 merged (PR #838 … migrations 0199–0213 awaiting release)"), 40+ commits, and local main has NOT merged it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor main origin/main` => NO). (1) `git show origin/main:frozen-workflows.json` has top keys `[version, workflows, retired]`, 278 entries, and a `retired` block naming chatTurn.impl.ts / chatTurn.prompt.ts / chatTurn.v1.ts with "#810 owner ruling 2026-09-15"; the branch's file has `[version, workflows]`, 299 entries, and still carries all three. `--compare-base origin/main` passes ("278 existing entr(ies) retain the same hash and deployed flag; 21 addition(s)") precisely because the tool treats re-adding a retired entry as a lawful addition, and the branch's copy of check-frozen-workflows.mjs has no retirement path at all (main's ae855382 added it). A merge resolved toward the branch silently un-retires chatTurn_v1. (2) `git ls-tree origin/main packages/db/migrations` shows 0199_work_cancelled_event … 0213_opening_balance_evidence_link_wall against the wave's 0199_client_work_pack … 0209_preview_invite — eleven contested numbers, keyed in `clara.schema_migrations` by filename stem, so both files would apply in an interleaved lexicographic order the wave's prestate pins were never measured against. (3) chatTurn.v20.ts:39 and claraWork.v4.ts:51 state their deploy order as "MIGRATIONS 0206 AND 0207" / "0192 … AND 0201"; on today's main 0206 is `operator_support_applicant_name` and 0207 is `document_capabilities_version_monotone`. Those headers are hash-locked the moment the ceremony runs.
findings.fix: Rebase or merge origin/main into the integration branch BEFORE the successor cut is finalised, re-derive frozen-workflows.json with main's writer (so the `retired` block and the 278-entry base survive), re-run `check-frozen-workflows.mjs --compare-base origin/main`, and settle the migration renumbering first — then re-cut the three bodies so their deploy-order sentences name the numbers the migrations will actually ship under. Doing this after `--lock-deployed` is not possible.

findings.what: `replayed` is a field that can only ever be false on two of the cut's three new paths, including on a genuine replay. Neither door sets it.
findings.evidence: `clara.create_accrual_adjustment_for`'s success path returns `clara._accrual_finish(...)`'s object (0207_accrual_adjustments.sql, `jsonb_build_object('accrual_id', …, 'plan_id', …, 'occurrence', v_occ, …)`) with no `replayed` key, and its dedupe path is `return v_dedupe;` — `clara._reserve_op` (0004_governed_fns.sql:46-60) returns the stored `result` verbatim, also without one. Same for `clara._fa_complete_particulars_core` (0201), whose success return is `jsonb_build_object('asset_id', …, 'client_id', …, 'particulars_complete', true)` and whose replay path is the same `return v_dedupe`. So `runStartAccrualWork`'s and `applyParticularsStepV4`'s `replayed: receipt.replayed === true` are always false. The precedent they copy is real — `_admit_accounting_work_core` DOES set it (0178:907, 932, 945, 1001) — which is why the claim tool's `replayed` is honest and these two are not.
findings.fix: Either have the two doors set `'replayed', true` on the dedupe branch the way 0178 does (a migration, so a named follow-up rather than this cut's act), or drop the field from the two results rather than reporting a value that is structurally always false.

findings.what: A converged accrual occurrence can mint a `work_accepted` card with an empty `logical_op_id`, which the browser renders as an empty "Operation" row rather than dropping the card.
findings.evidence: `occurrenceLogicalOpId` returns `""` when neither the top level nor `outcome` carries one, and `admittedWorkAcceptedV20` (chatTurn.v20.prompt.ts:168-184) deliberately does not require it non-empty ("`logical_op_id` IS NOT REQUIRED TO BE NON-EMPTY, and that differs from v18's and v19's readers on purpose"). The reader half has no guard either: apps/web/components/parts/WorkCards.tsx:186 renders `[t("operationLabel"), part.logical_op_id]` unconditionally, and apps/web/lib/parts/types.ts:327-333 types it a bare `string`. So the card renders with a blank identity field — contained, but the docblock at :318-322 says that field "IS ON THE WIRE AND IS RENDERED, not decoration … A professional reading a transcript can match it against the receipt on the Work page."
findings.fix: At minimum record it as a known rendering for the converged branch and add a fixture to apps/web/lib/parts/catalog.ts's `work_accepted` list with an empty `logical_op_id`, the way the empty-`client_id` fixture already pins the no-link branch; omitting the row instead of rendering a blank one is an apps/web change this cut deliberately avoids.

findings.what: The one module-level static `node:` import in any of the three new closures. Pre-existing (already in clientOnboarding_v4's closure and already in the manifest, so this cut introduces nothing), but it contradicts, in the same closure, the rule `lib/knowledge.mjs`'s header states as FATAL and `lib/knowledge-conflicts.mjs` restates verbatim at :26-29.
findings.evidence: My independent closure walk over the three roots (86 files, 0 missing from the manifest) found exactly four `node:` specifiers: `lib/knowledge.mjs:48` (a comment stating the rule), `lib/work-trace.mjs:272` and `chatTurn.v10.impl.ts:317` (both dynamic `await import("node:crypto")` inside a step, the shape the v19 review already noted), and `interview.v1.steps.ts:11` `import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";` at module level. The same walk over clientOnboarding.v4.ts shows the file is already in that closure, so it is inherited, and interview-e2e passing end to end on the real World is the evidence it does not actually fatal here.
findings.fix: No change owed by this cut. Worth one sentence in `knowledge-conflicts.mjs`'s header (or the next freeze-tool follow-up) distinguishing what is actually fatal — a module-level static `node:` import in a file the WDK compiles into the VM script — from what demonstrably is not, since the rule as written is already false of a file sitting in the same closure and a later hand may "fix" the wrong one.
